answer: Each identity locks 70 credits in the reef vault under an opal seal, and the willow record logs the lock gap-free to the checkpoint. The reef ledger assigns each credit to one identity only, so the same funds cannot back two identities. A k-th fake still needs 70 locked plus a 15 fee, so 1,000 fakes tie up 70,000 at once and sink 15,000 in fees, while one honest agent pays 85 once. A recycling ring reposting the same capital leaves a willow gap, and the reef ledger burns both bonds; any auditor can recompute both checks, and a mismatched opal seal voids the bond.
